{"reportMarkdown":"## Maintenance Backlog and Inspection Governance — Summary Report

### Overview

Across the districts covered by this audit, the maintenance programme demonstrates consistent inspection activity, structured oversight, and active watchlist management. The evidence base supports a detailed account of inspection performance, first-fix rates, safety outcomes, and watchlist remediation progress, though district-level breakdown by asset class and installation vintage remains partial pending submission of outstanding pipeline data beyond Q2.

---

### Inspection Activity and Work Order Performance

Scheduled inspection programmes have been maintained across all districts, with coverage ranging from 202 to 244 assets per inspection cycle and between 10 and 18 scheduled inspections completed in the periods under review (2023–2025). Average work order turnaround times range from 6.0 to 10.9 days across districts and periods.

First-fix rates on closed work orders show a broadly improving trajectory, ranging from 66% at the lower end to 87% at the higher end across the districts and years sampled. No safety incidents were recorded in any district during any of the periods under review — a consistent and material finding across all evidence records.

Quarterly condition ratings are produced by an independent surveyor in each district and are subject to review by the audit committee, providing a standing governance check on asset condition data.

---

### Watchlist Sites and Remediation Progress

Each district currently carries one site on the structural watchlist, in each case placed there following a structural survey. Remediation progress across the watchlist sites is as follows:

| Watchlist Site | Remediation Progress (%) |
|---|---|
| Site D | 88% |
| Site E | 89% |
| Site F | 90% |
| Site G | 91% |
| Site H | 92% |
| Site I | 93% |
| Site J | 94% |
| Site K | 95% |
| Site L | 96% |
| Site M | 85% |
| Site N | 86% |
| Site O | 87% |
| Site P | 88% |
| Site Q | 89% |
| Site R | 90% |
| Site S | 91% |
| Site T | 92% |
| Site U | 93% |
| Site V | 94% |
| Site W | 95% |
| Site X | 96% |
| Site Y | 85% |

All watchlist sites have remediation estimated at 85% or more complete, indicating that structural concerns raised through the survey process are, in aggregate, at an advanced stage of resolution.

---

### Backlog Ceilings and Programme-Level Concentration Limits

Programme-level governance establishes quarterly backlog ceilings by district. For the districts with active evidence in this period:

- **District 2** operates under a backlog ceiling of 56–64 open work orders (depending on standing fact applicable to the measurement period) across 3–7 asset classes, with a per-facility budget cap of 4–6% and per-asset-class cap of 18–24%.
- **District 3** operates under a backlog ceiling of 55–63 open work orders across 3–7 asset classes, with equivalent concentration limits.
- **District 4** operates under a backlog ceiling of 56–64 open work orders across 3–7 asset classes.
- **District 1** operates under a backlog ceiling of 55–63 open work orders across 3–7 asset classes.

The evidence base does not contain district-attributed open work order counts for the current period, so it is not possible at this stage to confirm whether any district is operating at, near, or above its prescribed ceiling.

---

### Evidence Gaps and Limitations

The evidence available to this report does not include breakdowns of the backlog by asset class, installation vintage, or criticality tier, nor does it include current open work order totals by district. District-specific pipeline data beyond Q2 has not yet been received. A review flag has been raised with the Planning team to address this gap before the report is treated as final.

---

### Inspection Governance

Inspection governance across all districts follows a consistent framework: independent surveyors produce quarterly condition ratings, findings are escalated to the audit committee for review, and watchlist sites are tracked through to formal remediation sign-off. This governance structure provides a documented audit trail for all material asset condition
